Midvale Business Review — Regional Business
Two Delivery Firms Now Operating as One
By Emmett Frawley, Winslow
The combination of Alderton Delivery Services and Halstead Transport is complete, and one operation now handles the scheduled deliveries and pickups that the two companies previously carried out separately for business customers in the nine districts they both served.
For more than fifteen years, both companies had sent vans into those districts on separate schedules. Neighboring streets were often served on different mornings, and customers in outlying areas waited noticeably longer than those close to either distribution center. Halstead Transport had also run Saturday pickups, which Alderton Delivery Services never offered.
Customers do not need to take any action. Signed agreements, most of which run for twelve months, continue on their current terms until those terms end. No new paperwork is required, and charges will be reviewed only when an agreement comes up for renewal.
"All 34 drivers and office employees who worked for the two firms have been kept on," said Louise Brennan, the managing director. "The shared name will start appearing on vans and paperwork in March, but it will be added in stages over several weeks rather than all at once." Timings for a few of the longer routes will be examined again later in the year, and any changes will be announced well in advance.
[Route times and district information are posted at each distribution center counter and on the company's website.]

Ravenscroft Linen Services
For immediate release: February 18
Reduced-Rate Midweek Pickup Service for Smaller Business Accounts
BEXFORD, February 18 — Ravenscroft Linen Services announced today that a reduced-rate pickup service will be available to its business customers from March 2. --[1]--.
The reduced rate is offered to smaller business account holders, including guest houses, salons, and dental practices. Linen picked up on a Tuesday or a Wednesday is charged at 15 percent below the standard pickup rate, while linen picked up on any other day of the week is charged at the standard rate. No call to the office is required; an account holder selects the service on the account page of the company website. --[2]--.
"Our vans leave the distribution centers with space to spare in the middle of the week, and filling that space costs us very little," said Rachel Buckley, director of operations. "Crews and routes are the same on every pickup day, so a customer paying the lower rate receives the same service as before." --[3]--.
As an introduction, accounts on the reduced-rate service will also receive one additional midweek pickup at no charge through April 30. --[4]--. Standard rates for pickups on all other days of the week remain unchanged.
Media contact: Simon Ledbetter, 555-0148
Founded in 1994 with one laundry in Bexford, Ravenscroft Linen Services supplies laundered linen to business customers and now operates from eleven distribution centers across the region.

Street performers will appear in Woodgate Square this spring under a new program run by the Woodgate Square Management Office. Posted by Yvonne Pratt, 9:12 P.M., June 24
I have bought my glasses from Copeland Eyewear for years, always at the store nearest my apartment. It is the only one I can use, because I finish work at 6:30 P.M. and can never reach a counter earlier. The hinge on my frames snapped on Sunday.
I took them in this evening. The assistant explained that no repair work is done at that store. Handling of Repairs Sent Off the Premises
For customers, effective from June 1.
An item left for workshop attention is entered on a record card at the counter and held in the store until the weekly transfer round. The case and the original receipt are not needed.

A customer who needs an item sooner than that may ask, before that store's transfer day, for it to be sent to the Lowden Street store by next-day courier. An extra charge applies.
